source: writing-qc section 5 (tone for India and international recipients). Pick the profile by the recipient's locale and company type; when unsure use default.

default.name_use: first name when they sign with it
default.logistics: state only what the role needs (notice period for recruiters)

IN_startup.applies_to: India: startups, product companies, MNC tech
IN_startup.name_use: first name if they sign with it
IN_startup.logistics: notice period (30, 60 or 90 days is normal and recruiters ask), current city, relocation

IN_traditional.applies_to: India: traditional firms, PSU, government, some family businesses
IN_traditional.greeting: Dear Ms. <last name>, or Dear Dr. <last name>,

US.register: very short, confident but not boastful; numbers matter more than titles
US.logistics: work authorization and time zone if relevant; notice period only if asked

UK.logistics: work authorization and time zone if relevant

EU_formal.applies_to: Germany, Japan, some banks on first contact
EU_formal.name_use: surname with title until they switch

EU_direct.applies_to: the Netherlands and similar very direct cultures

always: Name the recipient's time zone for calls (mornings your time).
Write dates as 21 September, never 09/21 or 21/09.
Never mention salary in outreach; forms that ask use the stored answer in the form's currency.
Mirror how they sign their own posts or emails.

phrases_to_remove.phrase: I am having 5 years of experience
humbly request, your kind self, I would be highly obliged
